explains: Keywords are short words printed on a unit's sheet that mean one specific rule. There are deliberately few, and none of them is 'plus twenty percent against X'. Every keyword either unlocks an order, changes a physical property, or connects the unit to the court. (Quirks — the named behaviours the court hands the battle, for units and captains alike — live in data/quirks.json; the captain model itself is in data/captains.json. These are unit traits, which is a different thing: a trait is what a unit IS, a quirk is what its politics did to it.)

keywords.name: Can Brace
keywords.rule: May be given the BRACE order. While braced: speed 0, full refusal, +140 shock resistance, front arc only.
keywords.explains: This unit's weapons are long enough to make a horse stop. It is the most important keyword in the game — but note it only says CAN. A spear line that has not been given the order gets nothing.
keywords.readOnField: Butts in the earth, points level, absolutely still.

keywords.name: Deep Block
keywords.rule: Default ranks 8 instead of 4. May form the ring.
keywords.explains: Stands eight deep: enormous staying power, a narrow front, and it turns like a barn.

keywords.name: Shield Wall
keywords.rule: May use the shieldwall formation: tighter files, front shield +25 percent, +60 shock resistance, six-tenths speed.
keywords.explains: Trained to overlap shields so each man is partly covered by his neighbour. It only works while the line holds — below 300,000 cohesion the shield bonus halves, because the wall has stopped being a wall.

keywords.name: Mounted
keywords.rule: Horse speeds and horse mass. +90 per mille to be hit in melee (a horse is a large target). Feels refusal at full strength. Melee armour = (rider x 2 + horse) / 3. Pursues at 3.5x kill rate and double capture rate.
keywords.explains: On a horse. Faster than anything, heavier than anything, easier to hit than anything — and the one creature on the field that will not run onto a set spear point.

keywords.name: Shock
keywords.rule: Delivers shock on impact above 60 mm/tick closing speed. Loses 200,000 cohesion on impact and needs its ready time standing still to redress.
keywords.explains: Exists to hit things very hard, once. The important half is the second sentence: charging home wrecks your OWN order, so shock troops are a piston — charge, strike, wheel out, reform, charge — and every stroke costs a rider out and a rider back.

keywords.name: Feigner
keywords.rule: May be given the FEIGN order (difficulty 70).
keywords.explains: Drilled well enough to run away on purpose and come back. Almost nobody has this. It is the hardest order in the game, and a failed attempt spreads REAL panic to your own line, because your neighbours cannot tell a false rout from a true one either.

keywords.name: Evade
keywords.rule: On the SCREEN job, automatically withdraws when an enemy comes within 45,000 mm. No order, no courier, no heed check.
keywords.explains: Never accepts a fight it did not choose. This is what makes skirmishers work with no attention from you at all.

keywords.name: Shoot on the Move
keywords.rule: May shoot while moving at a 400 per mille penalty, instead of not at all.
keywords.explains: Trained to throw or shoot from the saddle. A unit that shoots while moving never has to stand still, so it can never really be caught — the answer to it is not on the field, it is at court: catch it with your own horse, or make its paymaster poor.

keywords.name: Stakes
keywords.rule: May be given PLANT_STAKES: 1800 ticks immobile, then refusal 800 over 9,000 mm in the front arc, kept while stationary, left behind forever if the unit moves.
keywords.explains: Carries sharpened poles and a mallet. Ninety seconds of standing still buys a hedge nearly as good as pikes — and unlike pikemen, these men keep shooting the whole time.

keywords.name: Pavise
keywords.rule: +30 armour against missiles in the front arc, while stationary only.
keywords.explains: A standing shield propped in the ground. Thirty points against arrows, four against a sword, and none of it works if you move a step.

keywords.name: Maul
keywords.rule: Sidearm-class hammer with penetration 60, +12 in the press.
keywords.explains: The stake-hammer doubles as the tool that opens tired men in plate. Not a bonus — just what a five-pound lead head does.

keywords.name: Armour Piercer
keywords.rule: Missile penetration 62 or higher.
keywords.explains: Goes through plate where a bow only rattles it. Fewer shots, but the shots count.

keywords.name: Standard
keywords.rule: Radiates steadiness to all friends within its steady radius. If destroyed, every friendly unit loses 250,000 morale at once.
keywords.explains: Carries something worth standing near — and worth taking.

keywords.name: Signal Source
keywords.rule: Units with line of sight to this unit, within signal range, receive orders in 20 ticks and cost no courier.
keywords.explains: Your voice. Where this stands is where you can be heard — which is why moving it is a strategic act and losing it is a catastrophe.

keywords.name: Bodyguard
keywords.rule: Will not leave the command post; ignores movement orders beyond 30,000 mm from it.
keywords.explains: These men have one job and they know it.

keywords.name: Irreplaceable
keywords.rule: Cannot be replaced between battles. If destroyed or captured, the court must resolve it.
keywords.explains: There is only one Crown Banner and only one saint's arm. Losing them is a story that continues after the battle.

keywords.name: Holy
keywords.rule: May ABSOLVE once per battle: +200,000 morale to one contingent, no courier, requires line of sight. If captured: army-wide -250,000 morale and a Church penalty at court.
keywords.explains: God is watching, and so is the bishop, and the bishop keeps accounts.

keywords.name: Non-Combatant
keywords.rule: Deals no melee damage. Routs below 400,000 morale instead of 150,000.
keywords.explains: Cannot fight and will not try.

keywords.name: Proud
keywords.rule: Descriptive marker: this unit's captain takes over-the-head orders especially badly. The insult rule itself lives in the heed table.
keywords.explains: These men belong to a lord, and the lord notices when you go around him in front of his own retinue.

keywords.name: Ransomable
keywords.rule: If this unit's captain is captured, he is worth a ransom priced by his standing at court.
keywords.explains: Noble prisoners are money. This is why pursuit is tempting and why pursuit is dangerous.

keywords.name: Mercenary
keywords.rule: Morale floor is 0 instead of 200,000 while the contingent's arrears are above zero.
keywords.explains: Hired men fight exactly as well as they are paid, and they know precisely what they are owed.

keywords.name: Will Simply Leave
keywords.rule: If arrears > 0: on every captains'-hand check (every 40 ticks), 25 per mille chance the unit withdraws from the field entirely.
keywords.explains: Not a morale penalty. They go home. The strongest wire between the treasury and the battlefield in the game, and deliberately brutal.

keywords.name: Fragile
keywords.rule: Morale ceiling capped at 600,000.
keywords.explains: Can never be more than two-thirds brave, however well the day is going.

keywords.name: Nimble
keywords.rule: Turn multiplier 1400 per mille or better.
keywords.explains: Turns fast, which wins the race to a flank — and flanking is a race, because the other fellow is trying to wheel and face you.

keywords.name: Fleet
keywords.rule: Speed multiplier 1150 per mille; fatigue multiplier 900.
keywords.explains: Faster and less tiring than other footmen. The whole counter to heavy infantry lives in these two numbers.

keywords.name: Press Fighter
keywords.rule: Takes no crowd penalty in the press and gains the reach inversion rather than suffering it.
keywords.explains: Fights at arm's length by choice. Loses the first six seconds badly and wins everything afterwards.

keywords.name: Armour Wall
keywords.rule: Body armour 88 or higher.
keywords.explains: Effectively immune to cuts and nearly immune to arrows. Vulnerable to hammers, hooks, mud, and its own exhaustion.

keywords.name: Terrify
keywords.rule: Missile fear multiplier 4000 instead of 1400.
keywords.explains: Kills almost nobody and frightens everybody — which, since morale is the real health bar, is often better.

keywords.name: Misfires
keywords.rule: 60 per mille chance per shot of destroying the crew.
keywords.explains: Gunpowder. Sometimes the tube wins.

keywords.name: Immobile
keywords.rule: Speed multiplier 150 per mille.
keywords.explains: Wherever you put it at the start is where it is.

keywords.name: Pursuer
keywords.rule: Pursuit kill rate 3500 per mille; capture chance +200 per mille.
keywords.explains: Rides down running men — which is where the ransoms come from, and where battles are actually decided in blood.
